title: Canada’s Immigration Backlog Falls to 1.51 Million as IRCC Finalizes 3 Million Files
excerpt: IRCC cut its inventory by 35,180 applications in September, but family sponsorships grew, and 22% of economic files are waiting for levels-plan space rather than a decision.
body:
• Canada’s immigration department finalized 3,001,860 applications in the first nine months of 2026 and cut its total inventory to 1,508,675 by September 30 — down 35,180 in September alone.
  • The permanent residence backlog fell to 707,405, but family-class files rose by 1,685 to 168,855, the only major stream that grew.
  • Work permit and study permit queues are now small — 24,970 and 24,910 files — while visitor visas, at 298,060, account for most of the temporary residence backlog.
  • For applicants, the key distinction: 22% of economic files are not stuck in processing but are waiting for space under the 2026–2028 Immigration Levels Plan.

Canada’s immigration backlog is shrinking — unevenly. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) finalized more than three million applications between January 1 and September 30, 2026, and reduced the number of files awaiting a final decision to 1,508,675, according to an IRCC update published on November 17 with data current to September 30. In September alone, the department finalized 311,510 applications and cut its inventory by 35,180.

What the numbers count

The inventory is every application IRCC has received and not yet finalized, across permanent residence, temporary residence and citizenship; IRCC rounds all figures to the nearest multiple of five. Inside that total sit two very different kinds of waiting. Some files are in active processing. Others are complete or near-complete but are, in IRCC’s words, “waiting for space” — held because the annual admissions targets in the federal Immigration Levels Plan limit how many permanent residents Canada can land in a year. Of the 250,010 economic permanent residence files in the inventory, 78% are in processing and 22% are waiting for space. In the family stream the split is 58% processing and 42% waiting for space.

Where the backlog fell

Permanent residence accounts for 707,405 of the waiting files, down 7,935 in September. Economic applications — Express Entry, the Provincial Nominee Program, the Atlantic Immigration Program and federal business programs — fell by 6,545 to 250,010, with 236,710 economic files finalized in the first nine months. Protection applications, covering protected persons, refugees and humanitarian and compassionate cases, fell by 3,075 to 288,540, the largest single block of the permanent residence inventory.

Temporary residence fell fastest in percentage terms, down 17,490 in September to 347,935. But its composition matters for Indian applicants and visitors: the work permit queue is down to 24,970 files and the study permit queue to 24,910, while visitor visas dominate at 298,060. IRCC finalized 2,292,410 temporary residence applications in the nine months, including 1,923,425 visitor visas.

The exception: family sponsorship grew

Family-class applications were the one major stream moving the other way, rising by 1,685 in September to 168,855, with 79,705 finalized so far this year. IRCC says applications for spouses, partners and children were processed in about 15 months over the year to September 2026, and that demand for the Parents and Grandparents Program remains higher than the number of spaces in the levels plan, which lengthens waits; the department points eligible parents and grandparents to the super visa as the interim route.

What this means if you have a file in

A pending application is not necessarily a delayed one. If your file is in the share “waiting for space,” it moves when levels-plan room opens, not when an officer works faster. Two IRCC programs are also pulling people out of the temporary queues: the In-Canada Workers Initiative is transitioning up to 33,000 work permit holders already in Canada to permanent residence across 2026 and 2027, on top of levels-plan targets, and a one-time initiative is processing up to 115,000 additional permanent residence applications from protected persons and their dependants in Canada over the same period. On service standards, IRCC says about 74% of Federal Skilled Worker and Canadian Experience Class applicants received a decision within the six-month standard in the year to September 2026. Applicants can follow IRCC’s published processing data on its application processing system page, and CIC News tracks the monthly inventory releases stream by stream.

Citizenship: 245,900 new Canadians

The citizenship inventory fell 2.1% in September to 453,335 files — 322,650 citizenship grant applications and 130,685 applications for proof of citizenship certificates. Canada welcomed 245,900 new citizens in the first nine months of 2026, 27,940 of them in September.
